title: Three signals, one decision: intent, purpose, behaviour
lede: Every call is asked three separate questions. Only the deterministic tier can refuse; the scored signals alert or ask a person. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

nodes.label: Intent: what is it trying to do?
Purpose: was it ever in scope?
Behaviour: does this agent do this?

steps.title: The agent sends a call
steps.what: A tool call arrives with the agent key and its arguments.

steps.title: Intent is asked
steps.what: The request is classified by what it is trying to do, not only by what it literally says.

steps.title: Purpose is asked
steps.what: The key's declared purpose is compared with the call: tool, record count, data class, or no declaration at all.

steps.title: Behaviour is asked
steps.what: The call is scored against this agent's learned pattern. Not enforced until a baseline is established.

steps.title: A pattern match is a hard finding
steps.what: A deterministic pattern, such as a bulk export or a payee change, goes to the tier that may refuse.

steps.title: A purpose finding is a hard finding
steps.what: Outside the declaration, breaking one axis of it, or a key with no purpose.

steps.title: Similarity is a scored signal
steps.what: How close the text is to a risky intent. It can alert or ask. It cannot deny.

steps.title: Anomaly is a scored signal
steps.what: How far the call departs from the baseline. It can alert or ask. It cannot deny.

steps.title: Hard findings can deny
steps.what: Only this tier produces a refusal, with a reason code.

steps.title: Scored findings ask a person
steps.what: Above the ask threshold the call is held for approval. Above the alert threshold it goes through and an alert is raised.

steps.title: Allowed calls reach the MCP server
steps.what: If nothing refused and nobody is being asked, the call is forwarded.
